territorial_scope.description: Federal tax credit under the United States Internal Revenue Code.

evidence.quote: is an amount equal to 30 percent of the qualified investment

summary.short: Adds a 30% federal income tax credit (new IRC §48F) for qualified investment in agricultural technology projects producing specialty crops with precision or controlled environment agriculture, placed in service before 31 December 2035. Allows elective payment and transfer of the credit.
summary.long: Adds Internal Revenue Code section 48F, a credit of 30% of qualified investment in an innovative agricultural technology project for each taxable year. Qualified investment is the basis of depreciable tangible property or software used integrally in a project, placed in service during the year. A project is an agricultural technology or system placed in service before 31 December 2035 whose primary purpose is producing, storing, processing or packaging specialty crops using precision or controlled environment agriculture. Definitions include sensors, robotics, and software with machine learning or artificial intelligence; the Secretary may add technologies. Process-expenditure rules and a bar on double benefit for certain grants and EQIP payments apply. Section 2(b) and (c) allow taxpayers other than entities already covered to elect payment (IRC §6417) for property placed in service after 31 December 2023, and make the credit transferable (§6418). Section 2(d) makes conforming amendments to §§46, 49 and 50 and the table of sections. The amendments apply to property whose construction began after 1 January 2025. The bill contains no penalty or enforcement provisions.
